# Texts of the Quiz. Placeholders such as {k} are filled per question; the full list is in # apps-src/error-rates-dev/PLAN.md (section "Quiz mode"). Strings written r"(...)" are raw: # backslashes in them are typed once, as in LaTeX, e.g. r"(\(\alpha = 0.05\))". qs <- list( na = "Not answered.", go = "Try it in Explore", # ---- Quiz: feedback, all types ---- # {r}, {m}: rows answered correctly, and rows asked fb = c(ok = "Correct.", no = "Incorrect: {r} of {m} rows correct."), # ---- What changes ---- chg = list( # {chg}: the change, from `chg` below; {note}: from `note` q = "What happens to the following if {chg}? {note}", note = r"(
(One answer per row. Think of what happens on average, over many trials.))", # The effect size has its own sentence, for the compound with the larger (up) or smaller (down) effect qeff = c(up = "Suppose you test two compounds with the same sample size and significance level, and one has a larger true effect than the other. For the compound with the larger effect, how do the following compare with the other? {note}", down = "Suppose you test two compounds with the same sample size and significance level, and one has a larger true effect than the other. For the compound with the smaller effect, how do the following compare with the other? {note}"), # Per change, an increase (up) and a decrease (down). n: {n1}, {n2}; alpha: {a1}, {a2}; bonf, tests: {k} chg = list( n = c(up = "the sample size increases from {n1} to {n2} patients", down = "the sample size decreases from {n1} to {n2} patients"), alpha = c(up = r"(you increase the significance level from \(\alpha = {a1}\) to \(\alpha = {a2}\))", down = r"(you decrease the significance level from \(\alpha = {a1}\) to \(\alpha = {a2}\))"), bonf = c(up = r"(you apply a Bonferroni correction to {k} tests, each at \(\alpha = 0.05\))"), tests = c(up = r"(you run {k} tests at \(\alpha = 0.05\) instead of one, without correction)")), opt = c(up = "Larger", down = "Smaller", same = "The same"), row = c(fp = r"(Chance of a false positive (if \(H_0\) is true))", fn = r"(Chance of a false negative (if \(H_0\) is false))", fwe = r"(Chance of at least one false positive if every \(H_0\) is true)", sd = "Spread in outcomes of patients", se = "Standard error of the mean", w = r"(Width of the \((1 - \alpha)\) confidence interval)", sh = "Share of patients whose change lies inside the confidence interval", p = r"(\(p\)-value of a given trial)", avg = "Estimated drop in blood pressure"), # Appended to fp and fn for the changes with several tests each = " (per test)", # Feedback per row: {row}, {key} (from `opt`), {mis} (from `mis` below, or empty), {why} (from `why` below) fb = c(ok = "{row}: {key}. {why}", no = "{row}: {key}. {mis}{why}"), # Why each row's key holds, for either direction of the change. bonf, tests: {k}, {f0} and {f1} (the chance of at # least one false positive among k tests of true null hypotheses, in %, without and with correction) why = list( n = c(fp = r"(If \(H_0\) is true, the chance of a false positive is \(\alpha\), which you choose; the sample size does not change it.)", fn = "The more patients, the smaller the standard error, and the less often a real effect is missed: power grows with the sample size.", sd = "The standard deviation describes how much patients differ from each other. With more patients it is estimated more precisely, but that doesn't make patients more alike.", se = r"(\(\mathrm{SE} = s / \sqrt{n}\): the more patients, the smaller the standard error.)", w = "The more patients, the smaller the standard error, and the narrower the interval.", sh = "With more patients, the mean has greater precision. The interval will therefore be narrower, and a smaller share of patients will be inside it.", avg = "The estimates are centered on the true drop at any sample size; more patients only bring the estimates closer to it."), alpha = c(fp = r"(If \(H_0\) is true, the chance of a false positive is \(\alpha\) itself.)", fn = r"(The larger \(\alpha\), the easier it is to reject \(H_0\), and the less often a real effect is missed.)", se = r"(The standard error, \(s / \sqrt{n}\), does not involve \(\alpha\).)", w = r"(The confidence level is \(1 - \alpha\). With larger \(\alpha\), the procedure has lower confidence, and individual intervals will be narrower.)", p = r"(The \(p\)-value is computed from the data alone; \(\alpha\) is only the threshold it is compared with.)", avg = r"(\(\alpha\) only sets the threshold for rejecting \(H_0\); it does not change the data or the estimates.)"), bonf = c(fp = r"(Each test is done at \(\alpha / {k}\) instead of \(\alpha\), so each has a smaller chance of a false positive.)", fn = r"(Testing at \(\alpha / {k}\) makes it harder to reject \(H_0\), so real effects are missed more often.)", fwe = r"(Among {k} tests of true null hypotheses, the chance of at least one false positive is \(1 - 0.95^{{k}}\) = {f0}% without correction, and {f1}% with it, never more than 5%.)"), eff = c(fn = r"(Power grows with effect size: The larger the drop, the further it lies from \(H_0\), and the easier it is to reject.)", sd = "The size of the true drop shifts all patients by the same amount, so how much they differ stays the same.", se = r"(The standard error, \(s / \sqrt{n}\), depends on the spread and the sample size, not on the size of the effect.)", w = r"(The width depends on the standard error and \(\alpha\), not on the size of the effect: the interval only shifts.)", avg = "The larger the true drop in blood pressure in the population, the larger the estimates in samples tend to be."), tests = c(fp = r"(Each test still has a chance of \(\alpha\) of a false positive; the number of tests does not change that.)", fn = "Each test is the same as before, and so is its chance of a false negative.", fwe = r"(Among {k} tests of true null hypotheses, the chance of at least one false positive is \(1 - 0.95^{{k}}\) = {f0}%, compared with 5% for one test.)")), # Misconceptions, by change and row, named by the wrong answer for an increase (swapped for a decrease) mis = list( n = list(fp = c(down = "The sample size changes the chance of a false negative, not of a false positive."), sd = c(down = "It is the standard error that depends on the sample size, not the standard deviation."), sh = c(same = "A confidence interval is not a range that holds a fixed share of the patients: it shows where the true mean plausibly lies.")), alpha = list(w = c(up = "A higher confidence level needs a wider interval, not a narrower one.")), bonf = list(fn = c(down = "A correction lowers the chance of false positives at the cost of more false negatives.", same = "A correction lowers the chance of false positives at the cost of more false negatives.")), tests = list(fp = c(up = "It is the chance of at least one false positive that rises, not the chance per test."))), nan = "Please answer every row."), # ---- Quiz: results table below the question; `lab`: one column per question in `qz` (app.R); `end`: shown when all are correct ---- done = "Results", lab = c(sd = "SD and SE", err = r"(error rates and \(n\))", alpha = r"(error rates and \(\alpha\))", p = r"(\(p\)-value and \(\alpha\))", eff = "effect size"), end = r"(You answered every question type correctly at least once! Click here to go to the next chapter: Simple Linear Regression.)" )
